children: has withdrawn from a planned Nscale

data center in Loughton, Essex, adding uncertainty to the British AI infrastructure provider’s effort to raise as much as $3 billion through an initial public offering, the Telegraph newspaper reported. The project has faced delays linked to electricity constraints, although Nscale

said it remains committed to the Essex development and is considering alternative power supplies alongside other U.K. expansion locations. The company described its broader relationship with Microsoft
as strong and said the grid problems affecting the London area had no impact on its other contracts.

The UK setback follows delays at Nscale’s flagship Norwegian facility. Bloomberg News previously reported that the project was six months behind schedule, with 6.4 megawatts operating out of an intended 30 megawatts. Together, the projects illustrate the difficulty of converting demand for AI computing into usable capacity.

belongs to a growing group of specialized cloud providers building facilities to serve technology companies’ AI ambitions. Their expansion depends on substantial financing for equipment and construction, leaving them exposed when delivery schedules slip or investors become less willing to supply capital.
Recent market developments suggest that financing environment is becoming more difficult. Rival CoreWeave’s

shares fell about 25% during the week covered by the report as concerns persisted over borrowing needs across the sector. Australian data center developer Firmus also abandoned an IPO after failing to attract sufficient demand at its proposed share price.

planned listing will test investor appetite for businesses whose growth depends on infrastructure still under development. Securing dependable electricity, meeting construction milestones and retaining major customers are becoming central measures of whether those expansion plans can deliver.

title: Microsoft exits Nscale U.K. data center deal as IPO pressures mount
